newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight steady at 8.7 pct, liquidity improves.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight steady at 8.7 pct, liquidity improves.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 8.7 percent as liquidity improved by fresh injection of funds by the Malaysian central bank, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said agents of Bank Negara capped the overnight rate at the current level after lending earlier in the one-month market on behalf of the central bank.
No confirmation was available from the central bank, which does not usually comment on its open market operations.
Earlier, interbank rates eased across the board due to the big bank lending.
By 0345 GMT, one-month money had slipped to 8.0 percent from 8.5 at the open, three-month fell to 7.8/8.1 percent from 8.3 and six-month to 7.5 percent from 8.0/3.
One-week money was being lent at 8.2 percent against 8.7 at the open.
"It looks like Bank Negara is still injecting funds into the market," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past week to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange reversed a morning uptrend to trade marginally lower in late afternoon due to shortcovering, futures dealers said.
At 0850 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was down one at 92.38, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
The December contract was down one at 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
